title: Book One · Chapter 56: Six and Six
story:
Mum visits Mrs Lan after breakfast. The envelope is dry. Mum can read more of the writing now. But part of one word is still grey and unclear.

They put Dad's address card beside it. The numbers are the same. The street words are not.

“West Lane,” Ronan reads from their own card.

On the envelope, Mum can make out East and most of Court. The name above it is Gao.

“Mrs Gao,” Mrs Lan says. “That sounds right. I knew a woman with that name farther back. I last saw her a long time ago.”

“Then we found her,” Leo says.

“We found a name,” Mum says. “We still need the right person and door.”

Leo looks disappointed. They found a name, not a person. Ronan looks at the address again. Where is Mrs Gao's home? Ronan looks back at his map.

At school, he draws two big sixes on a spare page. Under one he writes WEST LANE. Under the other he copies EAST COURT from Mum's note. He circles the street words, not the numbers.

“Draw two green gates, too,” Leo says. Mrs Lan remembers a green gate at the other address. That gate was green a long time ago. It may be different now. Ronan puts a question mark beside it.

Jun comes to look. “Did someone try to steal the letter?” Jun asks.

“No,” Leo says. “They took it to the wrong door.”

“On purpose?”

“We don't know,” Ronan says.

“My cousin hid a note once,” Jun says. “He did not want to do the job.” Could this man be like that cousin? Leo begins to agree, then looks at Ronan's two sixes.

“Or he saw a green gate and a six,” Leo says.

Jun points to his cousin's story. Leo points to the two gates. But neither boy was there for the delivery. Ronan turns the page over. He does not want others to repeat those guesses.

Miss Wu hears their talk. “Is this class work?” she asks. They explain briefly. “This is someone's private letter,” she says. “Please do not make it a class game.” The adults can follow the address.

The address is private. Ronan puts the page away. Mum can check the address after school.

After school, Mum takes him past Mr Qiu's stall. She shows the copied outside writing, not the envelope. Bo's father is Mr Han. Mr Qiu knows him. Could this be his letter? “Mr Han pays small amounts back to Mrs Gao sometimes,” he says. She buys small things for his family.

Ronan takes a quick step. “Possibly,” Mr Qiu says again. “You need to ask him first.”

Mr Han isn't at the bun shop that afternoon. Mum keeps the address copy in her hand. Then she folds it into her notebook.

At home, Mrs Lan opens her front-room desk. She puts the envelope in its top drawer. The drawer locks. Mrs Lan shows Mum the drawer. “The envelope is here,” she says. Ronan stays beside Mum. He does not open the drawer himself.

He adds words to the map. He writes EAST COURT. Below it he writes ENTRANCE NOT CHECKED. The phrase is long and leaves little space for another shop.

Dad reads it after dinner. “That entrance still needs a check. Your note makes that clear.”

Ronan traces the unbroken road to their own gate. He can read both sixes easily. He checks the street words, too. Both sixes stay on the page. He can compare the street names under them. Those words make the addresses different.
studyGuide:
---

重点表达：drawer＝抽屉；locks＝锁得上；letter＝信件；address＝地址。

理解问题：

1. West Lane 的六号和 East Court 的六号为什么容易混淆？
2. 哪些观察还不足以证明送信人做错的原因？
